decision.title: The XPath front end (packet )
decision.summary: src/xpath_parse.c builds the XPath AST in one iterative tree-sitter cursor walk, applies the delimitation and lookup-key checks, and parses sequence types as () instance of T.

body.p: . src/xpath_parse.c builds the AST of in one iterative walk of a tree-sitter cursor in source order; the current AST parent is kept through the AST's own parent links, so nesting depth costs no C stack (20,000 nested parentheses pass under the wasm preset). Node types and field names map to kinds and fields through sorted static tables; the AST capacity is ts_node_descendant_count of the top node.

item.p: Checks of in the walk: A.3.2 delimitation over the terminals in order (non-delimiting: keywords, ncname, prefixed_name, uri_qualified_name and the numeric literals; a comment separates) and a prefixed_name in the key field of lookup or unary_lookup. Every failure, and the first ERROR or MISSING node, is XPST0003 with a static description, the source name, line, codepoint column and byte offset. With these, XP40 has no false rejects or false accepts left (32,542 valid queries build; Lookup-156 and MapConstructor-025a, the two false accepts, now fail).

A sequence type is parsed as the type of () instance of T: the prefix is served before the text through a TSInput callback (no copy), the result must be that instance-of expression with the type starting in the text, and spans are relative to the text.
tree-sitter aliases each token of alias(seq('(', ')'), jroot_selector) separately; the front end makes one JROOT_SELECTOR spanning both.
maximum_expression_depth counts AST nodes from the root (depth 1).
The only memory taken from the request's allocator is the AST, one allocation; tree-sitter's parser, tree and cursors use malloc ().
AST builder tests are in tests/xpath_ast_test.c (module prefix xpath, ), front-end tests in tests/xpath_parse_test.c.
